newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies open mixed, marks lower and yen up.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies open mixed, marks lower and yen up.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed in early quiet trade, with September marks lower and yen up.
Traders said cash cross activity was the feature, as mark/yen continued to deteriorate.
Traders noted dollar/mark was well-bid after early U.S. data. The latest weekly U.S. jobless claims fell to 332,000 in the June 21 week from a revised 346,000 in the prior week.
"Marks are still decidedly lower here, but in a kind of nowhere range until we hit $0.5819 to $0.5815 or $0.5831 on the upside," an IMM currency futures trader said.
Another trader, a floor manager of an IMM brokerage firm, said key support in September marks was $0.5812 to $0.5815.

"Mark/yen got below 67 and kept sliding, so once again that's the feature," the trading floor manager said. He noted good followthrough initially on the upside in yen, but said trade had already turned rangebound this morning.
September yen remained within Wednesday's range, but at session highs so far Thursday.
Sterling and Canadian dollar were firm, each reversing from losses on Wednesday.
Traders noted scant followthrough in futures pits from overnight news.
The Bundesbank left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged at its regular meeting.
Bundesbank Council member Reimut Jochimsen said he would not rule out another Bundesbank rate cut, but said that he did not see one.
Jochimsen also warned that prospects for European monetary union (EMU) were being threatened by a lack of political integration and said EMU "hangs in the balance."
One trader called the Jochimsen comments "a wash."
Early in the U.S. session, the APICS business outlook index fell slightly for the second month in a row, declining to 52.4 in June from 53.0 in May.

At 0812 CDT/1312 GMT, September yen was up $0.000017 at $0.008898, marks fell $0.0015 to $0.5821, Swiss francs fell $0.0008 to $0.7020, sterling rose $0.0026 to $1.6622, Canadian dollars rose $0.0078 to $0.7288 and Mexican pesos were $0.000125 lower at $0.121300. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
